jobs.title: Director of Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
MaintainX is a leading mobile-first work execution platform
for industrial and frontline teams. More than 13,000 customers
, including Duracell, McDonald's, Shell, DHL and Volvo, use MaintainX to cut unplanned downtime and run better operations, across 13.9 million managed assets and 79.5 million completed work orders.

In August 2026 MaintainX became part of Autodesk, joining
Autodesk Operations Solutions
, the organization unifying Autodesk's operations platform alongside Tandem, FlexSim and Fusion Operations.
Autodesk's strategy is to converge design, make and operate into one continuous lifecycle: design an asset, build it, run it, then feed what you learn running it back into the next design. Autodesk had design and make. Operate is the phase that tells you what actually happened, and it is ours.

The Opportunity

We're looking for an Engineering Director to lead MaintainX's Platform division. Platform owns the seven foundational teams every product engineer builds on: AI Builder, DevOps, Compliance, Testing Frameworks, Backend Frameworks, Mobile Frameworks, and SRE. This is a manager-of-managers role for someone who wants to define how a high-growth engineering org operates at scale.

What You’ll Do

Own the roadmap and operating model for Platform Engineering: set division-level priorities, manage cross-team dependencies, and translate business goals into multi-quarter platform investments.
Lead and develop a team of Software Development Managers - coaching on people development, technical judgment, and organizational effectiveness across seven teams.
Set the engineering standards every product team depends on: framework conventions, reliability targets, compliance posture, and CI/CD health.
Drive MaintainX's AI-native platform strategy - the AI Builder team's agent orchestration, tool registry, and developer environments sit in this division; your job is to ensure the org extracts real leverage from them.
Own division-level reliability: SLO definitions, incident response frameworks, on-call health, and the systemic path from incident to prevention.
Partner with the CTO and peer engineering leaders on org design, architectural decisions, and headcount planning.
Represent Platform Engineering to the business — translating infrastructure investment into engineering velocity, developer experience, and customer trust.
An expert level of English, both spoken and written, is required, as the individual will need to lead platform engineering managers across multiple teams, present technical priorities to executive stakeholders, and align with engineering leaders outside Québec on a daily basis.

About You

10+ years in software engineering with 5+ years in engineering leadership, including 2+ years managing managers across multiple teams.
Technical depth in at least two of: distributed systems, backend or mobile frameworks, platform engineering, reliability engineering - credible enough to make hard hiring decisions and engage in architecture reviews.
Track record of owning platform or infrastructure-focused teams at a growth-stage B2B SaaS company, with demonstrated impact on engineering velocity.
AI-forward: you set direction for teams building on LLMs and agentic workflows, and you hold your org to an AI-native standard.
Systems thinker who identifies organizational bottlenecks and eliminates them without creating new ones — you design teams, not just manage them.
Strong communicator who can represent platform complexity and tradeoffs clearly to product, finance, and executive stakeholders.

Nice To Have

Experience leading a Testing Frameworks, Quality Engineering, or Developer Productivity platform function.
Hands-on history scaling developer platforms through rapid headcount growth (Series D+).
Familiarity with CMMS, IoT, or industrial SaaS domains.

Our mission is to keep the physical world running.
Factories, fleets, hospitals and campuses stay up because the people who maintain them have tools worth using. That is what we build.

Compensation and benefits.
Base pay is one part of the package. Depending on the role, compensation may also include commission, an annual bonus and equity. Benefits differ by country. For roles in the United States, Autodesk’s benefits are described at benefits.autodesk.com. For roles in Canada and other countries, the plan differs on health coverage, retirement and leave, and your recruiter will walk you through it.

Belonging.
We take pride in a culture where everyone can thrive. More at autodesk.com/company/global-belonging. More on where this is going: Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost on building the future of connected operations, and AOS SVP Stephen Hooper on welcoming MaintainX to Autodesk.

Compensation Range: CA$173K - CA$254K

jobs.title: Director, Planning & Inventory
jobs.description:
“Join us in
building Careers and shaping Experiences Beyond the Box”

About Us

At Atlantic Packaging, every box tells a story and yours begins here. As a proudly Canadian-owned company with over 80 years of excellence in the corrugated packaging industry with operations within North America (Ontario, Quebec and United States), we’re committed to sustainability, customer excellence and community impact. Since 1945, we’ve supported local jobs and built a legacy of trust with our clients and team members. At Atlantic, your ideas matter, your growth is supported and your work makes a real impact.

The Opportunity

The Director of Planning & Inventory will lead the Ontario Corrugated team’s supply and inventory planning function to ensure customers receive their desired product at the service level they expect. Reporting to the Vice President of Supply Chain & Strategy, this role is critical for building organizational planning capability to support sustainable, profitable growth. It ensures alignment between business strategy and operational execution across production, procurement, and distribution.

The Director of Planning & Inventory leads a team of managers, planners and analysts with a focus on driving structure, establishing best practices for planning tools and processes, and driving continuous improvement initiatives to enhance forecast accuracy, machine utilization, inventory efficiency, and overall supply chain responsiveness.

What You’ll Do

Oversee the development and execution of the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP/IBP) process, ensuring alignment between demand, capacity, and financial plans across the organization
Direct inventory strategy to balance customer service levels with working capital objectives, minimizing excess/obsolete stock while preventing stockouts
Oversee supply planning and production scheduling alignment, ensuring plans reflect realistic capacity, lead times, and material availability
Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing planning team, including senior managers, plant-floor schedulers and inventory analysts
Partner with Sales and Business Performance teams to ensure the demand forecast can be utilized most effectively for capacity planning
Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Finance, Mills, and Sales to resolve supply-demand imbalances and support integrated business decision-making
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) — including forecast accuracy, scheduling compliance, inventory turns, fill rate, and on-time in full delivery — and drive corrective action where targets are not met
Lead continuous improvement initiatives to enhance planning maturity, process efficiency, and responsiveness to demand volatility
Provide senior leadership with visibility into planning risks, opportunities, and trade-offs to support strategic decision-making

What You Bring

The ideal candidate brings strong analytical and leadership skills, deep expertise in demand and supply planning methodologies, and a track record of driving results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Required

Undergraduate degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field
Certificate in Supply Chain Management considered an asset; APICS/ASCM,CPIM, CSCP or CPF
Experience building tools in PowerBI considered an asset
8+ years of progressive experience in demand planning, supply planning, or inventory management, including 3–5+ years in a leadership role
Strong track-record of developing high-performing teams while overseeing day-to-day operations
Proven experience leading S&OP/IBP processes in a manufacturing environment
Proven experience in improving capacity/demand planning processes, inventory efficiency, and service levels in a complex, fast-paced environment
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Excellent analytical skills with an ability to manipulate large data sets and present analyses in a clear, concise manner
Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate data into actionable business insights for various groups of stakeholders
Demonstrated continuous improvement mindset with the ability to identify metrics related to business processes, improving results through effective processes
Demonstrated proficiency in time management

What We Offer

Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage (dependents included)
Teamwork-focused culture with sustainability initiatives and social events
A culture of appreciation through a point-based recognition
Opportunities for advancement and internal movement
Education assistance for continuous skill development
Academic scholarships for employees’ children
Safety equipment and PPE support program
Retirement savings and wellness initiatives
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Inclusion and Accessibility

Atlantic Packaging is committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible and respectful environment for all candidates. If you require accommodation during the hiring process, please contact our Talent Acquisition team—we’re here to support you.

We sincerely thank all applicants for their interest in joining Atlantic Packaging. While we appreciate the time and effort invested, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Please note

Candidates who are 18 years or older are required to complete a criminal and background check. Details will be provided through the application process.

jobs.title: Director, Commercial Strategy
jobs.description:
Job Description

Director, Commercial Strategy

Amica Support Office, Downtown Toronto

Full-Time

3 days in Office (Mon-Wed)

Amica embraces pay- for- performance compensation philosophy and offers a competitive total compensation package designed to reward performance.

Expected Salary Range : 
$124,000-155,000

Maximum Bonus Potential :
20% target bonus, that rewards exceptional performance.

Benefits:
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage, retirement plan contributions, disability, and employee wellness programs.

Vacation:
Generous annual vacation entitlement, aligned with company policy.

Compensation is determined based on skills, experience, and qualifications. Candidates whose experience surpasses the expectations for this role may be eligible for compensation above the advertised range.

About Us

Amica is setting a new standard for senior living in Canada by combining unparalleled premium hospitality and amenities with expert care and support to deliver a personalized senior living experience. Committed to enriching the lives of seniors now and as their needs change, Amica offers Independent Living (IL), Assisted Living (AL) and Memory Care (MC) lifestyle options. Established in 1996, the company operates over 33 residences in British Columbia, and Ontario, with plans to continue expansion in select markets.

The Opportunity

The Director, Commercial Strategy is a senior commercial leader accountable for accelerating occupancy performance across Amica's pre-open, lease-up and occupancy-challenged residences. This role is focused directly on these priority residences - establishing commercial strategy, driving disciplined execution, removing barriers to performance, and partnering with Operations, Sales and Marketing to deliver occupancy results.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director acts as an enterprise commercial performance leader for priority residences and provides hands-on support to regional and residence teams. The role also leads selected enterprise commercial effectiveness initiatives that strengthen sales execution across the portfolio.

This position requires strong executive presence, commercial judgment, a bias for action, and the ability to move seamlessly between strategy and hands-on field execution.

What You Will Be Doing

Occupancy Performance - Pre-Open, Lease-Up & Occupancy-Challenged Residences (85%)

Own the commercial performance strategy for pre-open, lease-up and occupancy-challenged residences, with clear occupancy, sales, pipeline and conversion objectives.
Diagnose the commercial drivers of underperformance and translate them into focused residence-level action plans with clear priorities, owners, timelines and expected outcomes.
Establish and lead a rigorous performance cadence for priority residences, including regular business reviews, action tracking, escalation of barriers and executive reporting.
Partner closely with Regional Operations, residence leaders, Sales and Marketing to strengthen lead generation, pipeline health, conversion, pricing and promotional strategy, referral development and local market execution.
Provide hands-on commercial leadership to challenged residences, including direct coaching and challenge of frontline sales teams, targeted field support and decisive intervention where performance is off plan.
Own pre-open and lease-up commercial readiness and execution, ensuring each residence has the demand generation, sales capability, pipeline and market activation required to achieve occupancy milestones.

Performance Intervention & Recovery

Identify emerging occupancy risk early and mobilize targeted interventions before performance materially deteriorates.
Develop and drive 30/60/90-day recovery plans for occupancy-challenged residences, ensuring actions are practical, measurable and executed with urgency.
Challenge existing go-to-market approaches where results are not materializing. Recommend and, with the COO and functional leaders, drive decisive changes to sales resources, pricing, promotions, marketing investment, lead generation, referral strategy and local commercial execution when performance remains off plan.
Coordinate cross-functional support around priority residences and ensure teams remain focused on the few actions most likely to change occupancy trajectory.
Capture and scale successful practices from high-performing pre-open, lease-up and recovery situations across the portfolio.

Commercial Effectiveness & Field Enablement

Support sales force deployment, structure and resourcing decisions based on portfolio priorities and residence needs.
Lead sales incentive compensation strategy and execution, ensuring incentives reinforce enterprise occupancy and commercial objectives.
Partner with Sales and Marketing leaders on CRD capability, sales training and targeted development needs identified through residence performance.
Support CRM and sales process effectiveness, with a focus on field adoption, disciplined lead management and consistent execution.
Assess the effectiveness of key commercial initiatives and recommend where to continue, adjust or redirect investment.

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Commerce, Marketing, Hospitality, or a related discipline; equivalent relevant experience will also be considered.
8-10+ years of progressive commercial, sales, operations, or revenue leadership experience, ideally in a multi-site consumer, hospitality, seniors living, real estate, or service-based organization.
Demonstrated track record of personally driving measurable revenue, sales and/or occupancy improvement, with clear examples of materially changing the trajectory of underperforming businesses or locations.
Significant experience directly leading, coaching and challenging frontline sales teams; equally comfortable working alongside teams in the field and operating in the executive room.
Experience developing and executing turnaround or performance recovery plans for underperforming locations, including diagnosing root causes and translating them into decisive commercial action.
Experience supporting new openings, market launches, lease-up or other high-growth environments is strongly preferred.

Skills & Capabilities

Commercial operator: Strong instinct for what drives occupancy and revenue, with the ability to quickly identify where performance is breaking down and what needs to change.
Execution-oriented: Moves readily from strategy to action and maintains urgency, accountability and follow-through until performance improves.
Sales leadership: Strong understanding of the full sales funnel, lead management, conversion, referral development, relationship selling, closing and sales leadership.
Performance turnaround: Able to assess an occupancy-challenged residence, establish a focused 30/60/90-day recovery plan, mobilize the right resources and drive measurable improvement.
Market and pricing acumen: Comfortable assessing competitive positioning, pricing, promotions, customer demand, local market dynamics and barriers to purchase.
Cross-functional leadership: Able to bring Operations, Sales, Marketing and other partners together around a clear commercial plan without relying solely on positional authority.
Field orientation: Willing and able to spend meaningful time in residences, working directly with GMs, CRDs and regional leaders rather than managing performance primarily from the corporate office.
Judgment and decisiveness: Knows when incremental improvement is insufficient and can recommend and drive more significant changes to sales resources, pricing, promotions, marketing investment or local execution.
Performance literacy: Comfortable using funnel, conversion, occupancy and financial information to diagnose performance and make decisions; does not need to be an analytics specialist.
Executive communication: Strong presence and ability to communicate performance, risks, actions and recommendations clearly and succinctly to senior leadership.

Working Conditions

Primarily office-based role
Regular interaction with senior leadership, operational leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders across the organization.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment.
May require travel to residences, or off-site business meetings and planning sessions.
May be required to work additional hours during peak business periods, including annual operating plan development, forecast cycles, and board reporting periods.
Operates in a dynamic, fast-paced environment requiring adaptability, responsiveness, and sound decision-making under pressure.

What You Can Expect From Us

A diverse and inclusive environment where individual differences are celebrated, and you’re encouraged to be your best self
Collaborative environment where we work together to succeed as a team
Learning and development opportunities to help you grow
Comprehensive benefit package including RRSP matching
Office is centrally located in the financial district, on the PATH and the TTC subway line, and provides easy access to downtown amenities
Some travel required ( Hybrid work model, in office 3 times a week

At Amica Senior Lifestyles we are passionate about working together in a supportive and inclusive environment that fosters innovation and turns ideas into action. We remain committed to creating workplaces that reflect the communities in which we operate.  We are actively seeking applicants from all religions and ethnicities, LGBTQ2s+, Black, Indigenous, racialized people, and persons with disabilities and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply for our positions. 

Requests for accommodation can be made at any stage of the recruitment process providing the applicant has met the Bona-fide requirements for the open position. Applicants need to make their requirements known when contacted.
